chunks: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Kathīr narrated from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام that he said:

“When four things become widespread, four things appear: when fornication spreads, earthquakes appear; when zakat is withheld, livestock perish; when rulers act unjustly in judgment, rain is withheld from the sky; and when covenants are violated, the polytheists are given victory over the Muslims.”

key_terms.الذِّمَّةُ: covenant, protected obligation, or pledged security that must not be violated
key_terms.الزَّكَاةُ: zakat; the obligatory alms-tax whose withholding brings harm
key_terms.الزَّلَازِلُ: earthquakes; a worldly affliction mentioned as a consequence
key_terms.الزِّنَى: fornication; illicit sexual relations spreading in society
key_terms.الْحُكَّامُ: rulers or judges who exercise authority in public affairs
key_terms.الْقَضَاءِ: judgment or adjudication; the sphere in which injustice occurs
key_terms.الْمَاشِيَةُ: livestock; animals that perish when zakat is withheld

ai.seo_question: What worldly consequences does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام mention for social sins and injustice?
ai.summary: This hadith links widespread moral and social corruption with visible worldly consequences. It warns that fornication, withholding zakat, injustice in judgment, and violating covenants bring collective harm upon society.
